newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains ease in active trade as sterling firm.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains ease in active trade as sterling firm.

text.p: LIFFE grains eased in active trade as sterling staged a partial recovery against other European currencies.
Activity was boosted by profit taking by long holders on the old crop, one trader said. And on the new crop there was still good shipper buying, he said.
Active May wheat last traded 0.65 stg lower at 101.35 stg. May volume was 309 of a total 1,035 lots on wheat.
November was the most active barley contract, with 56 lots of a total 66. It last traded 0.25 stg lower at 94.50 stg.
Sterling tracked a rise in dollar/mark higher and was bolstered by interest rate rise expectations following firm UK jobs and retail data.

On a technical basis LIFFE wheat looks to be attempting to form a base, according to analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge. "If May clears 102 stg the move could extend to 110 stg in the short term," Gifford said earlier in the day in a technical summary.
"Support looks important immediately below 98 stg now," she said.
"Against this background the rally in barley could well extend," she said.
